summary: Drawing on Srila Rupa Goswami's Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu (Nectar of Devotion), Indradyumna Swami explains that of the 64 items of devotional service, five are singled out as the most essential limbs (angas): chanting Hare Krishna, hearing Srimad Bhagavatam, worshipping the deity, living in or visiting a holy place, and associating with devotees. He argues that sadhu-sanga (association with devotees) is the most essential of the five because it draws the essence out of the other four, comparing it to salt that brings out the flavor of every dish. Although chanting the holy name is the yuga-dharma that anyone can perform to remove sinful reactions and material desires, attaining prema requires receiving the mantra from a bona fide guru and chanting congregationally in the association of devotees. Each of the other limbs likewise depends on hearing from pure devotees: the Bhagavatam must be heard from a Vaishnava, since hearing it from impure professional reciters is like drinking milk poisoned by a serpent's lips; deity worship and knowledge of Krishna's personal features come only through the guru-parampara; and the transcendental glories of the holy dhama are revealed not by sightseeing but by hearing from saintly persons, for 'we see through our ears, not our eyes.' He illustrates these points with personal stories of Srila Prabhupada and Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati, and cites Sarvabhauma Bhattacharya's verses declaring that one is cured of the snakebite of material existence by chanting the names of Bhagavan in the company of Vaishnavas. He concludes that because Krishna consciousness cannot be perfected in isolation, Prabhupada founded ISKCON so devotees could associate, and that one should always honor devotees, beg forgiveness for offenses, and happily chant together.
key_points: Of the 64 limbs of devotional service in Rupa Goswami's Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu, five are most essential: chanting Hare Krishna, hearing Srimad Bhagavatam, deity worship, living in a holy place, and associating with devotees (sadhu-sanga) — and sadhu-sanga is the essence of them all.

Salt analogy: just as salt draws out the flavor of every food, the association of devotees draws out the essence of the other four practices; the speaker even travels with his own herbal salt and recalls Prabhupada eating an apple with salt in Vrindavan.

Chanting is the yuga-dharma and anyone can chant to be freed from sin and material desire, but attaining prema requires receiving the mantra from a bona fide guru and chanting congregationally; Jiva Goswami's Bhakti-sandarbha notes even a neophyte may feel a glimpse of ecstasy in kirtan, like sun breaking through clouds.

Bhagavatam must be heard from a Vaishnava: the speaker's story of walking into a University of Kentucky graduate class on Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu (1970-71) — the professor knew it intellectually but had no purifying effect on students. Hearing from the unqualified is like 'milk touched by the lips of a serpent.'

Deity worship depends on the guru-parampara revealing Krishna's personal features (flute, Vaijayanti garland, etc.); Prabhupada named it 'Krishna Consciousness' (not 'God Consciousness') to reveal the personality of Godhead, since one cannot love someone one does not know. Kichari story: Prabhupada's cooking tasted like Mother Yashoda's recipe.

To understand the holy dhama one must hear from saintly persons, not merely sightsee — 'we see through our ears, not our eyes.' Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati told disciples who left his lecture to see the arati that they 'just saw stone'; Prabhupada told a disciple who saw only rickshaw-wallas, pigs and open sewers in Vrindavan that a 'speck' (material desire) was in his eye.

Hearing from the guru is our lifeline, like the umbilical cord connecting child to mother; Prabhupada chastised the sleeping speaker in Hyderabad, saying transcendental sound (shabda-brahma) acts even without understanding the language, like taking medicine on a doctor's authority. Chanting plus devotee association together are potent like nitroglycerin (nitrogen + glycerin).
references: Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu (Nectar of Devotion) by Srila Rupa Goswami — source of the 64 items of devotional service and the five essential angas/limbs; also the text being taught in the university classroom story.
Bhakti-sandarbha by Jiva Goswami — cited for the importance of congregational kirtana, whereby even a neophyte devotee may experience ecstatic symptoms as an impetus to continue.

Srimad Bhagavatam 1.2.18-19 — paraphrased: by regularly hearing the Bhagavatam and rendering service to the pure devotee, all that is inauspicious in the heart is destroyed and irrevocable loving service to the Lord becomes manifest.
Sri Gurvastakam (Guru-astakam), verse 3 — cited that the spiritual master takes great pleasure in training devotees to dress the deities in beautiful ornaments, knowing what pleases the Lord.

Chaitanya-charitamrita — the pastime of Sarvabhauma Bhattacharya finding Lord Chaitanya unconscious in the Puri temple and composing 100 verses glorifying Him; one verse stresses that relief from the 'snakebite of samsara' comes through the medicinal herb of chanting the names of Bhagavan ('asadham bhagavan-nama') in the association and service of Vaishnavas ('srimad-vaishnava...').
Hare Krishna maha-mantra — quoted and discussed as the yuga-dharma, the sound to be chanted congregationally in the association of devotees.
Story of Srila Prabhupada naming the movement 'International Society for Krishna Consciousness' (1966) rather than 'God Consciousness,' to reveal the personality of Godhead.
stories: Salt on food — just as salt draws out the flavor of every dish, association with devotees draws out the essence of the other practices; the speaker travels with his own herbal salt and once saw Prabhupada eat an apple with salt in Vrindavan.

Blitzkrieg at University of Kentucky — the young devotee barged into a graduate class only to find the professor teaching Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu, yet with no purifying effect on the smoking, gum-chewing students.
Milk touched by the lips of a serpent — a snake sips the cooling milk on the windowsill and leaves its venom behind, like hearing Bhagavatam from an impure reciter.
The kichari that tasted like Mother Yashoda's recipe — Prabhupada cooked kichari so wonderful that a godbrother said he had never tasted anything like it.
Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati stops his lecture — when disciples left to see the arati he told them, 'you just saw stone; better you had sat and heard my lecture.'
The speck in the eye in Vrindavan — Prabhupada told a disciple who saw only rickshaw-wallas, pigs and open sewers that a speck of material desire clouded his vision of the dhama.

Sleeping in Hyderabad — Prabhupada chastised the drowsy speaker, insisting transcendental sound (shabda-brahma) acts even without understanding the language, like taking medicine on a doctor's authority.
Nitroglycerin — chanting Hare Krishna and serving in the association of devotees are each potent, but combined they are explosive like nitrogen plus glycerin.
quotes: We see through our ears, not through our eyes.
Milk touched by the lips of a serpent.
How can you love someone you don't know?
Why are you sleeping while I am talking?
